 Order
1.

Since these appeals arise out of the same award passed by the Claims Tribunal, they have been heard together and are being decided by a common order.
2.
These appeals under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

M.A.No.9955/2024 has been filed by the Insurance Company and M.A.No.1091/2025 has been filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29356 2 MA-9955-2024 award dated 24.10.2024 passed in Claim Case No.863/2017 by the 20th Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore whereby compensation of Rs.57,71,257 has been awarded to the claimants on the death of Pritam Singh.

sentences.text: 3. Short facts of the case are that on 28/11/20216 the accident occurred when deceased Pritam Singh (the deceased) going from Dwarakapuri to Fhooti Kothi by his motorcycle bearing registration No.MP 09.QQ.5808.

At the same time offending vehicle dumper (owned by respondent No.10)
coming from Hawa bungalow side bearing registration no. M.P. 09. G.G. 223, the respondent Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Charan Kaur on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81420252/
1 No.9/driver, driving the said vehicle rashly and negligently hit the deceased motorcycle.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Charan Kaur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Due to consequences of the accident deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
The incident was reported in the police station Dwarakapuri, district Indore.

4. The case of the Insurance Company is that the claims tribunal while considering the income of the deceased has taken his income based on Income Tax Returns Exhibit P/12 according to which the income of the deceased was Rs.3,58,556/-.

However, on bare perusal of Exhibit P/12 and the computation of income appended to the ITR acknowledgment it can be seen that there was a component of other income which related to interest accrued from Kisan Vikas Patra and SBI account to the tune of Rs.57,556/-.

He submits that this income would continue to accrue to the claimants hence while assessing the income for quantification of compensation for loss of dependency this component could not have been taken into account by the claims tribunal.

As regards the appeal of the claimants the claimants points NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29356 3 MA-9955-2024 out that there were 8 dependents of the deceased at the time of accident.
He submits that the dependents were widow, children and aged mother, father of the deceased.
He submits that claims tribunal has only considered the number of dependents at 6 while infact on the date of accident they were 8.
At the time of accident father was 70 years of age and mother was 69 years of age hence both were dependent on income of the deceased.

However,
both of them died during pendency of the claim petition before the tribunal.

Consequently, the claims tribunal excluded them and while making deduction for personal expenses has considered only six dependents and therefore, deduction at 1/4th has been done which in view of the law as laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 2017 ACJ 1770 SC should have been made at 1/5th because the number of dependents exceeding six.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 2017 ACJ 1770 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also points out that similarly only because of the death of parents during the pendency of the claim petition amount of compensation for loss of consortium has also not been paid to them.
He submits that if the deduction is made by 1/5th and amount of consortium is awarded to the parents also then there would be enhancement at around Rs.5,15,000/-.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Co. by repeating his submissions points out that in case the interest component is removed from the income of the deceased then there will be reduction of compensation in the head of loss of dependency at around Rs.9,00,000/-.
He thus prays for reduction of the compensation accordingly.

6. On bare perusal of Exhibit P/12, which is the Income Tax Return for NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29356 4 MA-9955-2024 the assessment year 2016-17 relevant to the financial years of 2015-16, it is seen that the income of the deceased was Rs.3,58,556/-.
This income was including the interest accrued from Kisan Vikas Patra and SBI bank account.
The contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Co. has substance that this interest shall continue to accrue to the claimants even after the death of Pritam Singh.

7. Similarly the contention of the learned counsel for the claimants has also found favour with this Court that number of dependents should have been considered at the point of time of death due to accident and not at the time of decision of the claim petition.

Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Charan Kaur on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81420252/
2 8.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Charan Kaur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the fact that in the case of reassessment after changing the deduction for personal expenses at 1/5th and adding amount of consortium and applying interest thereon from the date of filing claim petition before the tribunal, the amount which would be enhanced will be almost identical to the amount which will be reduced after removing the component of interest, this Court is of the considered view that no order for enhancement or reduction is required to be passed in both the appeals.
Hence, both the appeal are hereby disposed off in view of the fact that rival submissions have satisfied the claims raised by the contesting parties.

9. In view of the disposal of these appeals, the claimants are free to withdraw the amount deposited by the Insurance Co.
(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29356 5 MA-9955-2024 SS/-
